questions.question: When did the peasant movement in Bardoli begin?
questions.solution:
• Bardoli Satyagraha: 1928
  • Leadership: Led by Vallabhbhai Patel, this peasant movement against tax hikes earned him the title 'Sardar.'

questions.question: What was the meaning of ‘Ryot’ in British records in the 18th century?
questions.solution:
• Ryot: Peasants
  • Etymology: In British administrative records, Ryot (from the Arabic 'Ra'iyah') specifically referred to the individual cultivator or peasant.

questions.question: Who among the following kings founded the Maurya empire in ancient India?
questions.solution:
• Mauryan Founder: Chandragupta
  • History: With the help of Chanakya, Chandragupta Maurya overthrew the Nanda dynasty to establish the first pan-Indian empire.

questions.question: In which of the following years was the Vijayanagar empire founded?
questions.solution:
• Vijayanagara Year: 1336
  • Detail: The empire's capital was Hampi, now a UNESCO World Heritage site known for its stunning ruins.

questions.question: Bhaskaravarman of the Varman dynasty ruled in the ______ region.
questions.solution:
• Bhaskaravarman: Kamarupa
  • Dynasty: He was the most famous ruler of the Varman dynasty of Kamarupa (modern-day Assam) and a contemporary of Harshavardhana.

questions.question: Who was the ruler of Delhi sultanate when Ibn Batuta came in India?
questions.solution:
• Ibn Batuta's Arrival: Muhammad Bin Tughlaq
  • Traveler: The Moroccan traveler Ibn Batuta served as a Qazi (judge) in the court of Muhammad bin Tughlaq for several years.

questions.question: Who was appointed as the first Surveyor General of India in 1815?
questions.solution:
• Surveyor General: Colin Mackenzie
  • 1815: Colin Mackenzie was appointed as the first Surveyor General of India, known for his extensive mapping of South India.

questions.question: ______’s foster mother Mahapajapati Gotami was the first woman to be ordained as a bhikkhuni.
questions.solution:
• Buddha's Foster Mother: Buddha
  • Fact: Mahapajapati Gotami was the first woman to enter the Sangha, marking the beginning of the female monastic order in Buddhism.

questions.question: Which was the first empire in ancient India to use elephants in its war on a large scale?
questions.solution:
• War Elephants: Magadha
  • Military: The Magadha empire (particularly under the Nandas and Mauryas) was the first to integrate a massive elephant corps into their tactical operations.

questions.question: Which maharaja of Manipur signed the Instrument of Accession with the Government of India?
questions.solution:
• Manipur Accession: Bodhchandra Singh
  • 1947: Maharaja Bodhchandra Singh signed the Instrument of Accession, integrating Manipur into the Dominion of India.

questions.question: ‘Purusha Sukta’ is a hymn from which Veda?
questions.solution:
• Purusha Sukta: Rigveda
  • Scripture: Found in the 10th Mandala of the Rigveda, this hymn describes the spiritual origin of the universe and social order.

questions.question: How many storeys does Qutab Minar have in Delhi?
questions.solution:
• Qutub Minar Height: Five
  • Architecture: The minar has five distinct storeys, built using red sandstone and marble by different rulers over time.

questions.question: Who was the founder of the Mamluk dynasty in India?
questions.solution:
• Mamluk Founder: Qutb al-Din Aibak
  • Sultanate: He was a former slave of Muhammad Ghori and founded the Slave (Mamluk) Dynasty in 1206.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.option_1: In 1774, the Asiatic Society was founded by Sir Williams Jones.
questions.option_2: In 1775, the Siraj ud-Daulah was defeated in the Battle of Plassey.
questions.option_3: In 1776, the first railway service began from Bombay to Thane.
questions.option_4: In 1793, the Cornwallis code was enacted.
questions.solution:
• Correct Statement: In 1793, the Cornwallis code was enacted.
  • Correction: The Asiatic Society was founded in 1784; Plassey was in 1757; the first railway was in 1853.

questions.question: In the Battle of Swally (1612) the British fought against the ______.
questions.solution:
• Battle of Swally: Portuguese
  • 1612: This naval victory by the British over the Portuguese paved the way for the East India Company to establish a factory at Surat.

questions.question: Who among the following presided over the special session of Congress in September 1923 and at the age of 35 became the youngest man to be elected as the President of the Congress?
questions.solution:
• Youngest President: Maulana Abul Kalam Azad
  • INC: At 35, Maulana Azad became the youngest person to preside over a Congress session (Delhi, 1923).

questions.question: Hamideh Banu Maryam Makani was the wife of Mughal emperor ______.
questions.solution:
• Humayun's Wife: Humayun
  • Detail: Hamida Banu Begum was the wife of Humayun and the mother of the future Emperor Akbar.

questions.question: ‘Memoirs of Babur’ or ‘Baburnama’, also known as ‘Tuzk-e Babri’, was written by:
questions.solution:
• Baburnama: Babur
  • Literature: Written in Chagatai Turkic, Babur's autobiography provides a vivid description of the flora, fauna, and politics of Hindustan.

questions.question: In Indian history who were referred to as the 'atavika rajya'?
questions.solution:
• Atavika Rajya: Forest kingdom
  • Ancient India: This term was used (notably in Ashokan edicts) to refer to the tribal forest states that existed on the fringes of the empire.

questions.question: In which year did Gongsa Ugyen Wangchuck become the first monarch of Bhutan?
questions.solution:
• Bhutan Monarch: 1907
  • History: Ugyen Wangchuck was crowned as the first Druk Gyalpo, unifying the kingdom and establishing the current hereditary monarchy.

questions.question: In which of the following years did the Santhal Revolt take place?
questions.solution:
• Santhal Revolt: 1855-56
  • Rebellion: This was a massive tribal uprising in the Rajmahal hills against the oppression of local zamindars and British policies.

questions.question: In which year did Akbar analyse the state revenue statistics for the last 10 years, which contained information on price fluctuations and land productivity?
questions.solution:
• Dahsala System: 1580
  • Akbar: After studying ten years of revenue data, Akbar and Todar Mal introduced the Dahsala (ten-year) system of land assessment in 1580.

questions.question: Where were the terracotta models of the plough excavated in Harappan civilisation?
questions.solution:
• Banawali Site: Banawali
  • Archaeology: Located in Haryana, Banawali is famous for yielding high-quality terracotta models of Harappan ploughs.

questions.question: Who among the following started the construction of the Qutub Minar?
questions.solution:
• Minar Construction: Qutb al-Din Aibak
  • Architecture: Aibak started the first storey, but the monument was completed by his successors Iltutmish and later Firoz Shah Tughlaq.

questions.question: In 711 CE, Arab general ______ conquered Sind, which became a part of the Caliph’s domain.
questions.solution:
• Arab Conquest: Muhammad Bin Qasim
  • 711 CE: The 17-year-old general Muhammad Bin Qasim defeated Raja Dahir, bringing Islamic rule to the Indian subcontinent via Sindh.
